messages:
Alex Kim: Quick question — contractor (ext-analytics) needs read-only access to logs in redwood-prod for ~48h to triage a spike. Data may include PII, so want least-privilege + audit trail. What's the recommended pattern?
Ria Patel: Don’t give Project Viewer. Best is a narrow custom role scoped to only the BigQuery dataset (redacted logs) and the exported logging resources they need. Prefer service-account impersonation for human access (no long-lived key).
Sam O'Neill: Agreed. For human investigators we usually: create a service account, give it a custom role with only required permissions, and allow impersonation for a short window. Also add an IAM Condition to enforce expiry.
Ria Patel: Example flow: create custom role with logging+bigquery read perms, bind to sa, then allow `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` to the operator who will impersonate, or grant `iam.workloadIdentityUser` for federated auth. Quick sample to create role (example):
```
gcloud iam roles create tempLogReader --project=redwood-prod \ 
  --title="Temp Log Reader" \ 
  --permissions=logging.logEntries.list,bigquery.tables.getData,bigquery.jobs.list \ 
  --stage=GA
```
Then bind to a service account:
```
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod \ 
  --member="serviceAccount:sa-temp-logs@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \ 
  --role="projects/redwood-prod/roles/tempLogReader"
```
Sam O'Neill: For expiration use an IAM condition on the binding, e.g. `request.time < timestamp("2026-03-20T12:00:00Z")`. That avoids manual revocation.
Morgan Lee: I can provision this. Will: create a SA, create the custom role scoped to dataset `redacted_logs`, add binding with condition for 48h, and disable any long-lived keys.
sec-bot: Ticket #4523 opened: "temp access ext-analytics" — ownership: Morgan Lee, severity: low, require security review.
Alex Kim: Two additional constraints: 1) Contractor must only access the redacted dataset (no raw logs). 2) We need full audit logging of any queries they run against the dataset.
Ria Patel: Make sure the BigQuery dataset has row-level redaction already applied, or put the contractor on a view that masks PII. Also add `bigquery.auditLog` checks to the ticket.
Sam O'Neill: Implementation tip: avoid creating SA keys. Instead give the contractor `impersonate` access to the SA and share instructions to `gcloud auth print-access-token --impersonate-service-account=sa-temp-logs@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --duration=3600s`. That gives short-lived access and is easy to revoke.
Morgan Lee: Done — I provisioned `sa-temp-logs@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, created custom role `roles/tempLogReader` limited to `redacted_logs` dataset and logging list, added IAM Condition to expire in 48h, and posted impersonation steps to the ticket. No keys created.
Alex Kim: Awesome, thanks. I confirmed the dataset is a view over the redaction pipeline. Please add KMS audit and include encryption key access in the review.
Ria Patel: Added `@oncall-security` to the ticket for visibility.
Morgan Lee: Note in the ticket I attached the policy snippets and the exact condition timestamp. If anything else comes up ping me here or in the ticket.
Alex Kim: Works for me — thanks everyone :tada:
